newsitem.title: LIBERIA: Major party rules out boycott of Liberia poll.
newsitem.headline: Major party rules out boycott of Liberia poll.

text.p: The political party fielding the only woman for president in Liberia's July 19 election said on Thursday it did not plan to boycott the poll despite joining calls for a postponement.

The Unity Party of former U.N. official Ellen Johnson-Sirleaf stated its stand after attending talks with 11 others of the country's 13 political parties demanding a delay in the poll because of alleged irregularities in voter registration.
"We took part in these talks, but the Unity Party was not part of any call for a postponement. We will fully participate in the elections," said party spokesman Dusty Wolokolie.
Spokesmen for some of the parties threatened to pull out of the presidential and general elections, already pushed back from May 31 for logistical reasons.
The elections commission on Wednesday ruled out a poll delay, saying such a move would be a recipe for further trouble in the country emerging from seven years of civil war.

The Nigerian-led West African peacekeeping force ECOMOG, policing Liberia since 1990, on Thursday gave assurances of security for the elections. It said it would shut down any newspaper or radio station issuing unofficial results.

"Any radio station or newspaper that tries to announce the results of these elections before an official declaration is made will find itself closed and its staff locked up at my base," declared force commander General Victor Malu of Nigeria.
He said the measure was in line with a provision of the special laws guiding the conduct of the elections.

ECOMOG said, however, it had failed in its effort to bring together warlords and arch rivals Charles Taylor and General Roosevelt Johnson to heal a rift that plunged the capital Monrovia into militia warfare in April 1996.

There is an air of apprehension in Monrovia that victory by Taylor, a front-running presidential candidate, would trigger renewed fighting by Johnson's ethnic Krahn followers. Johnson is not a candidate but still commands significant following.
"Unfortunately, former general Roosevelt Johnson informed us at the last minute that he will not be here because of personal reasons," ECOMOG chief of staff General Abdul-One Mohamed told reporters.
